body:
Hello,

The problem you're running into is called 'ghost collision'. First of all, here's an updated node_3d.tscn that fixes the issue:

[node_3d.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18348664/node_3d.zip)

The changes are as follows:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/25b4bd98-a589-41bb-a819-0de76bbdca82)

* Red: I grouped all shapes under a single static body. Jolt does not support 'Enhanced Internal Edge Removal' across bodies, so they need to be combined:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3d890941-4afc-4c71-993a-707508f8ed63)

* Blue: I shortened the box so that the edge of the ramp (orange) exactly coincides with the edge of the block. Jolt only removes shared edges, it cannot reason about edges touching a surface or T-edges. If I go back to your original scene and pull the ramp apart a little, then the red dotted line indicates where there should have been an edge (obviously boxes don't support this):

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/407d84b1-e697-4559-9914-cfc9620ee92b)

My recommendations: Make the ramp a single mesh instead of building it from several parts.

You can reduce (but not eliminate) the chance of ghost collisions by tweaking the following two parameters:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ae045fb5-b256-421d-931b-08f40b7b2cc4)

* Speculative Contact Distance: This is the main thing that makes ghost collisions more likely to happen in this case:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e7e9a728-193e-448d-93a9-e9e869c6fbd6)

Zero turns this system off.

* Penetration slop: Reduces the amount the sphere can sink into the platform. Setting it to zero is possible but can have stability issues.

> The problem you're running into is called 'ghost collision'. First of all, here's an updated node_3d.tscn that fixes the issue:

I thought that the issue was the ball bumping into the lower edge of the ramp due to having sunk into the ground too much. I thought ghost collisions meant bumping on edges of perfectly connected bodies, which now that I say out loud, it does describe what is happening here, and the game is also getting issues with bumping on connected bodies so I'll have to rethink how I handle collision shapes.

> Red: I grouped all shapes under a single static body. Jolt does not support 'Enhanced Internal Edge Removal' across bodies, so they need to be combined:

The game is made out of modular pieces, so I'll probably have to write a system that combines the collision shapes at runtime

> My recommendations: Make the ramp a single mesh instead of building it from several parts.

In the test level from the actual project this wouldn't be entirely possible as the ramp was in the middle of a large (100m^2) plane. Something I thought of (which I ran out of time to properly test) is putting the ramp collision slightly under the ground like such, would this help?
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9871a9b1-2ab5-4ab0-8428-aede833adfe0)

> is putting the ramp collision slightly under the ground like such, would this help?

Yes it should.
